content_units: You have a credible 6-month path into   corporate Learning & Development   in Singapore, especially for roles that value   facilitation, curriculum design, stakeholder communication, and LMS usage  . With 7 years of teaching experience, your strongest angle is not “starting over,” but repositioning yourself as an   instructional design + facilitation + capability-building   professional.
Compensation reality:   a target of   SGD 5,500/month   is realistic for the right fit, especially in:
- L&D Executive / Specialist roles in larger firms
- Enablement or academy-style roles in tech, healthcare, finance, and professional services
Best-Fit Singapore Roles and Salary Outlook
Role   Fit for your background   Likely SGD/month   Gap to close   Hiring outlook
Learning & Development Executive / Specialist   Strong fit if role includes facilitation, onboarding, training coordination   4,800-6,500   Corporate metrics, stakeholder language   Good
Instructional Designer   Very strong fit if you can show adult-learning portfolio samples   5,000-7,000   Authoring tools, adult-learning framing   Very good
Training Specialist / Learning Facilitator   Strong fit for presentation-heavy roles   4,800-6,200   Corporate examples, business alignment   Good
Sales Enablement / Customer Training Specialist   Good fit if you can train adults and simplify concepts   5,500-7,500   Commercial context, product-training examples   Good
Talent Development Coordinator / Analyst   Moderate fit   4,200-5,500   HR systems, reporting, admin-heavy workflows   Fair
Organizational Development / Talent Management   Weaker near-term fit   5,500-7,500   HRBP/OD experience, change frameworks   Harder in 6 months
These are possible later, but less efficient for your first move:
- Organizational Development specialist roles requiring direct HR/change-management history
How to Reframe Your Teaching Experience for Corporate L&D
Option 1:   Instructional Designer     Strongest match if you enjoy designing learning journeys and assessments   Best leverage of curriculum design
Option 2:   L&D Specialist     Best balance of facilitation, program coordination, LMS work, and stakeholder engagement   Good route to SGD 5,500+
Option 3:   Training Specialist     Good fit if you want more live delivery, workshops, onboarding, and capability building   Fastest pivot story
Option 4:   Sales Enablement / Customer Education     Strong option if you present confidently and can teach systems/processes to adults   Higher upside pay
Translate school language into business language:
-   Curriculum design → Program design and capability development
-   Student assessment → Learning evaluation and measurement
-   Parent/department stakeholder management → Cross-functional stakeholder engagement
-   Differentiated instruction → Learner segmentation and audience adaptation
-   School LMS use → Learning platform administration and digital learning support
-   Pastoral/committee work → Change adoption, coordination, and communication
-   Exam performance tracking → Learning analytics and reporting
-   Assembly/presentation delivery → Workshop facilitation and executive-ready presentation
Keywords to use on your resume and LinkedIn

Learning & Development / Instructional Design Professional transitioning from education with 7 years’ experience in curriculum design, facilitation, LMS-supported learning, and data-informed performance improvement.
- You design and deliver learning, not just teach classes
- You can support adult learners and business teams
- You use data and feedback to improve outcomes
- You are comfortable with digital learning systems and structured content
Achievement bullets: how to rewrite them
Use this formula:   Action + scope + business-like outcome
- Taught secondary English to students across multiple levels
- Designed and delivered structured learning programs for diverse learner groups, adapting content to different proficiency levels and improving engagement and assessment outcomes.
- Developed curriculum-aligned learning journeys, assessments, and supporting materials to drive measurable learner progress across multiple cohorts.
- Used Excel to track student results
- Used Excel to analyze learner performance trends, identify intervention needs, and refine instructional strategies based on data.
- Collaborated with internal stakeholders to align learning content, assessment standards, and delivery timelines across multiple programs.
Even if unpaid, this helps a lot:
- Built a 30-minute onboarding module for new managers
- Created a microlearning series in PowerPoint/Canva/Articulate
- Designed a learning needs analysis template
- Produced a post-training evaluation dashboard in Excel
- Reworked a school curriculum unit into an adult-learning module
- Lead with outcomes, not teaching duties
- Mention   adult facilitation   anywhere you have trained teachers, parents, committees, or student leaders
- Put   LMS, Excel, PowerPoint, Google Workspace, assessment design   in skills
- If you know any authoring tool soon, add it prominently
Month 1   Reposition your profile   Rewrite CV and LinkedIn; map teaching experience to L&D keywords; identify 30 target employers   Corporate-ready CV + LinkedIn
Month 2   Build credibility fast   Learn adult-learning basics; create 2 portfolio samples; start light networking   Portfolio v1 + stronger pitch
Month 3   Close tool gaps   Learn one authoring tool; improve Excel reporting; practice interview stories   3-4 polished work samples
Month 4   Start focused applications   Apply to 20-30 targeted roles; tailor resume; contact recruiters; request informational chats   Active pipeline
Month 5   Interview conversion   Prepare case answers; refine salary story; improve portfolio walkthrough   Interview-ready package
Month 6   Land and negotiate   Prioritize best-fit roles; negotiate around scope and salary; accept role with growth path   Offer at target or near-target
- Rewrite your LinkedIn headline around   L&D, instructional design, facilitation
- Create a master resume with 8-10 strong achievement bullets
- Build a target list: banks, insurers, healthcare groups, universities, training providers, edtech, tech firms, consulting firms
- Start using a 30-second pitch: “I design and deliver learning programs, use LMS tools, and translate learner needs into structured training experiences.”
Month 2: Build evidence, not just intent
- Post or share one short LinkedIn reflection weekly on learning design, facilitation, or training effectiveness
Month 3: Close the most important gaps
- Learn basic   ADDIE  ,   Kirkpatrick  , and   adult learning principles
- Apply to   targeted roles only  , not broad HR roles
- Tailor each application to 6-8 keywords from the job description
- Reach out to recruiters in Singapore focused on HR, learning, and corporate support functions
- Message L&D managers and instructional designers for short conversations
- “How would you design onboarding for a new team?”
- justify through 7 years of design + facilitation + LMS + analytics
- If first offer is slightly low, negotiate on:
What Will Most Likely Get You to SGD 5,500+
Instructional Designer or L&D Specialist in a mid-to-large company   is the most realistic route to your pay target within 6 months.
Sales Enablement / Customer Training   can pay better, but you will need to sound comfortable training adults in business settings and possibly supporting product/process learning.
Lower-probability route for your salary target
Coordinator-level HR/L&D roles   may get you into the field but often land below your target.
